newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on Thursday on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.70/1.65 percent compared with last Tuesday's yield of 1.88/1.83 percent.
One-year treasury bills closed at a yield of 2.00/1.95 percent against last Tuesday's yield of 2.20/2.15 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.36/98.41 from last Tuesday's close of S$98.07/98.12, September 2001 at S$97.54/97.59 versus S$97.05/97.15 and June 2003 at S$95.54/95.59 against S$95.05/95.10.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from last Tuesday's 2-5/8 2-1/4 percent.
